stances_toward.note: The Alliance of Sahel States is the bloc Burkina chose after leaving ECOWAS: a pact signed in July 2024 with Mali and Niger (Al Jazeera headline; the exit from ECOWAS is dated January 2024, DW). The grade ally rests on the pact; the treaty text was not opened here, so whether it carries a defence clause is not verified. Bond affinity is our reading: the three juntas share a coup origin, the sovereignty frame and a hostility to ECOWAS and France, with no kinship. Two tier 3 sources only, so C. The MLI card reads the same pact as ally from its side.

stances_toward.note: The three juntas (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger) expelled French forces and moved toward Russia; the Africa Corps replaced France in Mali. In November 2025 France told its nationals to leave Mali as the JNIM blockade tightened, and in April-May 2026 the JNIM-FLA offensive threatened the junta in Bamako. Rival, not adversary: France has no aim to bring the juntas down. Bond - grievance (colonial and the 2013-2022 Barkhane period).

stances_toward.note: The Alliance of Sahel States is Mali's own confederation: a treaty signed at the Niamey summit in July 2024 with Burkina Faso and Niger, after the three juntas left ECOWAS. The grade rests on the treaty (Al Jazeera). Bond affinity is our reading: the three juntas share a coup origin and anti-French, anti-ECOWAS positions, with no kinship. Mirror: the FRA card reads the same bloc as rival (grievance); the AES side of that pair is not carded.

stances_toward.note: A rival bloc, not a partner: the AES left ECOWAS, called the sanctions 'inhumane and irresponsible', accuses Nigeria of meddling, and Burkina Faso's leaders threatened Nigerian aircraft over their territory (December 2025). Rival, not adversary: no source calls for the AES's destruction, and Abuja's stated aim is ECOWAS's survival with the AES back 'under a different status'. The exit's effective date is reported differently across sources; the year is recorded, not the day.

stances_toward.note: Lomé's April 2026 strategy aims to intensify political dialogue with the Sahel states (the AES) and to position Togo as their mediator. That is transactional cooperation with no alignment: partner, with no defence clause. Warming is our reading of the step from the 2021 plan to the 2026-2028 strategy. Bond none is our reading; no source names kinship or affinity. Gaps, not recorded as stances: Nigeria and ECOWAS (reluctant_partner, bridge role), Ghana and Benin (kin), France (partner, cooling) and China (partner, port) have no source opened in this pass that uses those readings; the AES membership question is not settled in any opened source.
